problem:
A numerical method is used to approximate the solution to an initial value problem.

- With step size $Δx=0.25,$ the observed local truncation error is $τ(0.25)=0.50.$

- With step size $Δx=0.10,$ the observed local truncation error is $τ(0.10)=0.01.$

Estimate the order of the numerical method.

feedback.problem:
A numerical method is used to approximate the solution to an initial value problem.

- With step size $Δx=0.08,$ the observed local truncation error is $τ(0.08)=0.13.$

- With step size $Δx=0.02,$ the observed local truncation error is $τ(0.02)=0.002.$

Estimate the order of the numerical method.
feedback.worked_solution:
A numerical method has order $p$ if $p$ is the largest positive integer such that the local truncation error (LTE) satisfies

$$
τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{p+1})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

The order describes how fast errors shrink as $Δx$ decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order $p$ if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of $k$ reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately ${k}^{p+1}.$

In our case, the step size decreases from $0.08$ to $0.02.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
k=\frac{0.08}{0.02}=4.
$$

As a result, for a numerical method of order $p,$ the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately

$$
{k}^{p+1}={4}^{p+1}.
$$

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from $0.13$ to $0.002.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
\frac{0.13}{0.002}=65.
$$

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{p+1} & ≈65 \\ p+1 & ≈{log}_{4}⁡(65) \\ p+1 & ≈3.011… \\ p & ≈2.011….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is $2.$
